name: libexosip
why: A door into SIP, the signalling protocol behind VoIP calls, with the eXosip toolkit as a way in.

brief.what_it_is: eXosip (libexosip, eXosip2) is a C library that the Savannah project page describes as hiding 'the complexity of using the SIP protocol for multimedia session establishment.' SIP is the signalling protocol behind VoIP calls. The page says it is mainly for VoIP telephony applications, endpoints or conference servers, but could also suit any application that establishes sessions, such as multiplayer games. I did not read the API or see what the library takes in or emits. The Savannah page names osip2 as the companion library and eXosip2 as a rewrite of the earlier eXosip.
brief.why_it_exists: The Savannah summary frames it as a way to use SIP for session setup without handling the protocol's complexity directly. The antisip.com vendor page says osip and eXosip2 were started in 2001 by the same team.
brief.install_notes: Not covered by the pages I read. The Savannah page links to Git, Subversion and CVS repositories and a download area, but I did not fetch them. The brew executables sip_monitor, sip_reg and sip_storm were supplied in the scout notes; I did not see them in any fetched page.
brief.standout: It is a long-lived, small, C-based SIP toolkit whose maintainers also sell commercial licences for osip2 and eXosip2 alongside the GPL release. The author's notes say it was 'a complete rewrite' of eXosip in 2006, which may matter if older documentation is found.
brief.status: quiet. The Savannah page lists the latest news as osip2 and exosip2 5.1.0, posted 28 Mar 2019. The 4.0.0 news is from July 2012. Development Status is listed as '6 - Mature'. The group has one active member. I found no 2020-or-later release or news item.
brief.caveats: I did not get a README or any usage docs from a repository, so command syntax, build steps and API details are missing from this brief. The antisip.com page is a commercial marketing site, not project documentation, and it describes the company's own SDKs. The Savannah project is licensed GPL v2 or later. The Savannah page calls itself 'The eXtended osip library', while the name in the scout notes is libexosip, so check the package name against the source before writing.
quotes: eXosip is a library that hides the complexity of using the SIP protocol for mutlimedia session establishement.
eXosip is also mature. However a few bugs around PRACK and retransmissions were reported and fixed.

links.label: Antisip (maintainer, eXosip2 SDK docs linked from here)

fetch_log: https://savannah.nongnu.org/projects/exosip: worked; a Savannah project summary page, not a README. Contains the description, license, status and news.
https://www.antisip.com/: worked; vendor marketing page for Antisip's SDKs. It mentions osip2 and eXosip2 but gives no usage docs. Not followed further.
